source_snapshot.procedure: Get sensor type through both IB and OOB using 0x04/0x2f, set sensor type through both paths using 0x04/0x2e, then get again through both paths.
source_snapshot.criteria: All commands complete without error and the sensor type is set correctly.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek/merged guidance reduces the test to generic `sensor info`, omitting the source's explicit Set Sensor Type mutation, both IB/OOB paths and get-set-get verification.

original_test_intent.purpose: Unresolved between a read-only OOB Get Sensor Type test named by the item and a state-changing dual-path get-set-get Sensor Type assignment test defined by the procedure and acceptance criteria.
original_test_intent.target: An unspecified BMC sensor number and its Sensor Type/Event-Reading Type assignment, potentially addressed through both host in-band and remote out-of-band interfaces; the exact mutable sensor and owning controller/LUN are not supplied.
original_test_intent.scope: The item/script name suggest one OOB Get 2Fh query. The procedure instead requires IB Get, OOB Get, IB Set 2Eh, OOB Set 2Eh, then both Gets again, while the criterion explicitly judges the set. These scopes cannot be merged without duplicating a mutation or redefining the test.
original_test_intent.operation: Do not execute until the owner chooses and corrects the row. A Get-only case would perform bounded 2Fh reads and SDR comparison. A Set/Get case would require one deliberately settable sensor, one approved type/code transition, exact path ownership, volatile/nonvolatile behavior, event/monitoring impact, one authoritative write path and restoration to the original assignment.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 10 attended and 5 machine minutes, but the procedure contains six commands and two Set operations with no statement whether both writes are required or duplicate the same mutation.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Unresolved. Get-only acceptance is a valid two-byte type/code read matching the current SDR. Set/Get acceptance requires the approved new assignment to appear through both paths, affect event semantics as specified, and restore correctly; command completion alone is insufficient.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Source-owner scope decision; exact sensor/SDR owner/LUN and settable capability; selected type/code and compatibility; IB/OOB routing equivalence; baseline type/code and event behavior; approval and recovery; exact per-path requests/responses; post-set and restored SDR/event/monitoring behavior; preserved logs.
ambiguities: Item says Get/OOB, while procedure and criteria require Set plus both IB and OOB.
The procedure writes the same assignment twice without defining whether IB and OOB target the same controller or whether a second write is meaningful.
No sensor number, settable capability, approved new type/code, persistence model, expected event impact or restore value is provided.
Looking up existing type/code and setting the same values would only test an idempotent write, not a transition, unless that is explicitly intended.
source_conflicts: The read-only title and merged command directly conflict with the mutating source procedure and `set correctly` criterion; removing the Set, as V2 did, changes the original requested activity.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 creates a safe and technically sound Get-only 2Fh reader, but it silently deletes the source's Set Sensor Type step, dual IB/OOB execution and set-verification criterion. This is prohibited scope reduction: the source conflict must be surfaced rather than resolved in favor of the title.

applicable_history.decision: No locked user decision authorizes dropping the Set steps or selecting a mutable sensor. Historical read-only treatment cannot override the source procedure/criteria conflict.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Block the current row because the item and procedure define materially different tests. V2's read-only rewrite is not intent-preserving. The owner must split a Get-only OOB case from any approved Set/Get round trip or explicitly choose one; only then can the correct FULL or REQUIRES classification be applied.

available_now: IPMI 2.0 defines Set Sensor Type 2Eh and Get Sensor Type 2Fh as distinct commands with known request/response fields.
Read-only BMC/SDR/sensor inventory and IB/OOB route identity can be collected without changing the sensor.
The standard notes that assignments may be volatile or nonvolatile and Get is mandatory when Set is implemented.
missing_inputs: Owner decision to keep Get-only, retain Set/Get, or split the row; corrected item/procedure/criteria/script mapping
Exact sensor identity/SDR owner/LUN, proof it supports Set Sensor Type, approved compatible new type/event-reading code and whether a real transition or idempotent set is intended
Whether both IB and OOB writes are required, how they map to one controller, assignment persistence and expected event/monitoring/SDR effects
Dedicated window, mutation approval, baseline/export, safe restore value and recovery when monitoring/events become inconsistent
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The testcase owner resolves scope; the BMC/sensor owner selects a settable sensor and valid assignment/persistence model; the lab owner approves mutation and recovery; the monitoring owner defines downstream evidence.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Inventory BMC/firmware, IB/OOB routes and current SDR/type/code; determine documented Set capability without transmitting command 2Eh.
Prepare separate Get-only and Set/Get contracts and validate parsers offline.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not issue Set Sensor Type through either path, choose a sensor/type from `sensor list -v`, drop source steps silently, perform two writes, clear logs, or assume IB and OOB reach the same sensor owner.
Do not infer that setting the existing value validates a type transition or that successful completion proves event/monitoring correctness.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The source is corrected or split; each row has one scope and explicit path list. Any Set case names a documented settable sensor, valid transition, persistence/effects, single-write authority, approval and restoration; a Get-only case removes all Set criteria explicitly.

revision_candidate.test_name: Owner Decision Required: OOB Get Sensor Type versus Dual-Path Set/Get Sensor Type
revision_candidate.purpose: Resolve whether the testcase is a read-only metadata query or a controlled sensor-type assignment test; do not execute until the source has one unambiguous purpose.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: No executable environment while scope conflicts. A corrected Get case needs verified BMC/sensor/SDR and OOB access; a Set/Get case additionally needs a documented settable sensor, dedicated window, both path mappings, approval and recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Pending mutually exclusive scopes: OOB Get only, or a separately approved get-set-get sequence over explicitly named paths. Never merge them implicitly or apply setters to an arbitrary production sensor.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Owner scope decision; corrected source; exact sensor/owner/LUN; support/persistence; valid type/code and expected effects; path mapping; baseline; approval; evidence and restoration/recovery plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Do not send 2Eh. Collect only read-only inventory and return SOURCE_CONFLICT. After correction, re-review either a bounded `raw 0x04 0x2f <sensor>` read or a controlled one-write assignment followed by IB/OOB verification and restoration; preserve the selected scope exactly.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Source conflict resolved; target sensor and routes verified; for mutation, Set capability, valid assignment, expected behavior, persistence, workload impact, approval and recovery documented; logs preserved.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Owner correction and exact scope; Get case: raw two-byte type/code and SDR match. Set/Get case: baseline, signed new assignment, one exact Set, both-path read-back, event/monitoring consequences, persistence decision, restoration and non-target health.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Intel IPMI 2.0 rev. 1.1 sections 35.15-35.16/Tables 35-16 and 35-17, Tables 42-2/42-3, exact SDR/platform documentation and corrected owner decision.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never guess a sensor/type/code, write an ordinary non-settable sensor, duplicate a mutation through both paths, clear evidence, ignore event semantic changes, omit restoration or reduce the source to Get without an owner correction.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Owner scope decision is mandatory. If Set remains, fresh BMC/lab/monitoring approval is required for the exact sensor, assignment, path, persistence and restore plan.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners resolve source intent and judge valid sensor reassignment. After correction, reads and approved bounded write/read-back can be automated; impact and exceptional recovery remain human decisions.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Undefined until scope selection. A Set case must restore the original type/code through the authoritative path, confirm event/monitoring recovery and escalate without repeated writes if restore fails.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved Get-versus-Set scope; missing sensor/capability/type/code/path mapping; production sensor risk; absent approval/recovery; duplicate write; command error; read-back mismatch; event/monitoring anomaly; failed restore; or any attempt to clear logs.

identified_defects: V2 removes the explicit Set Sensor Type actions and thus changes the original test purpose.
Source title/script/merged command specify Get-only while procedure and criteria specify a mutating dual-path round trip.
The procedure can issue the same mutation twice without path/ownership semantics.
No safe target, valid assignment, persistence/effect or restore contract exists.
reason_for_change: Apply the user's SOURCE_CONFLICT rule instead of V2's silent scope reduction. Set Sensor Type changes sensor and event semantics and can be volatile or nonvolatile; it cannot be discarded merely because the item name says Get, nor executed from an ambiguous dual-path recipe.

new_technical_evidence.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7 Markup
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Sensors/controllers implementing optional Set/Get Sensor Type
new_technical_evidence.supports: Set 2Eh assigns Sensor Type and Event/Reading Type and may be volatile or nonvolatile; Get 2Fh retrieves the two fields and is mandatory for sensors supporting Set. These are distinct mutation and read operations.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The intended scope, target sensor, Set support, valid assignment, path mapping and persistence remain unresolved.

removed_ambiguities: Makes the Get-versus-Set contradiction explicit instead of hiding it.
Separates IB/OOB verification paths from write authority.
Requires a real assignment intent and restoration rather than blindly re-setting listed values.
resolved_blockers: None for execution; normative evidence confirms that V2 omitted a distinct mutation.
remaining_blockers: Owner must correct or split the source and, if Set remains, supply a safe target, valid assignment, approval, expected effects and recovery.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 prevents a false review PASS created by deleting the core mutating steps and protects against two unapproved sensor-type writes to an unspecified device.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The restored source conflict and prohibition on silent Get-only reduction are queued for isolated validation.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source performs Get through IB/OOB, Set through IB/OOB, then Get through both again despite the Get/OOB title.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 keeps only one 2Fh read and removes the 2Eh writes and set acceptance.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Permit only inventory and source reconciliation; no 2Eh write until the owner resolves scope and supplies a settable target, assignment and recovery.
